title: A natural field experiment on the effectiveness of economic sanctions before and after the Russian invasion of Ukraine
title_zh: 俄乌冲突前后经济制裁有效性的自然实地实验
abstract: Abstract Here, using two rounds of natural field experiments based on an audit-study approach, we investigated whether sanctioned Russian government officials retain access to the international financial system. Researchers sent 7,081 email solicitations to intermediary firms in 202 countries and jurisdictions to establish shell companies and set up corporate bank accounts. Responses to sanctioned names (middle initial modified) are compared with equivalent solicitations from non-sanctioned placebo names. Round 1 results in December 2020 reveal no statistically significant difference in financial access for the sanctioned names compared with placebo. Round 2 findings in May 2022, after the Russian invasion of Ukraine, indicate that sanctioned individuals’ access to international corporate services and banking was significantly reduced (drop in non-compliant response rates: 4.0 percentage points, 95% confidence interval 1.2–6.8, P = 0.006, Cohen’s d = 0.207). The results suggest that factors related to the war and not sanctions law proved decisive in constricting sanctioned individuals’ access to the global financial system.
abstract_zh: 摘要：在此，我们利用两轮基于审计研究方法的自然实地实验，调查被制裁的俄罗斯政府官员是否仍保持对国际金融体系的访问权。研究人员向202个国家和司法管辖区的7,081家中介企业发送了电子邮件，旨在设立壳公司并开设企业银行账户。对制裁名字（中间名修改）的回复与等价的安慰剂组邀请进行比较。2020年12月的第一轮结果显示，与安慰剂组相比，制裁名字在财务获取方面没有统计学上的显著差异。2022年5月的第二轮结果，在俄乌冲突后，表明被制裁个人的国际企业服务和银行业访问权显著降低（非合规回复率下降4.0个百分点，95%置间1.2–6.8，P = 0.006，Cohen’s d = 0.207）。结果表明，与战争相关的因素而非制裁法在限制被制裁个人的全球金融体系访问权方面起了决定性作用。
